real.title: What if ChatGPT is recommending your competitors instead of you
Twelve clients. Twelve deadlines. One board

carousels.hook: Hand these 5 jobs to AI and you'll lose clients
carousels.caption:
Hand these 5 jobs to AI and you'll lose clients

Yes, AI makes work faster. But get some jobs wrong and clients never come back:

1. Replying to an angry client
2. Setting prices and negotiating
3. Promising deadlines
4. The final check before delivery
5. Owning the client relationship

One rule: AI writes the draft, you make the call.

Which job do you never give to AI? Tell me in the comments, and save this post.

carousels.hook: I stopped asking “what do I post today?”
carousels.caption:
I stopped asking “what do I post today?”

The problem was simple: generic AI tools don't know my brand and don't remember what I've posted.

So I built myself a Content OS: structured context, strategy from history, a fixed design engine and automatic QA.

Now the system answers the question. My job is to build and share it.

Save this for the next build log.

carousels.hook: New SaaS? What I'd do in the first 30 days
carousels.caption:
New SaaS? What I'd do in the first 30 days

Launch day isn't the finish line. The real work starts then, and most of it is talking to people.

Days 1-7: find the first 10 users by hand
Days 8-14: fix where users get stuck
Days 15-21: take the first payment
Days 22-30: turn what worked into stories

Every week, AI makes the job faster: call notes, repeat questions, reasons for no, one story into several posts.

Which week are you in? Tell me in the comments, and save the plan 🚀

carousels.hook: Do more without hiring more people
carousels.caption:
How do you get more done without hiring?

A small team's real problem isn't headcount. It's doing the same work by hand every week.

1. Find the repeat work
2. Write the steps on one page
3. Give writing and research to AI
4. Keep the final check yourself

And teach AI your business once: keep prices, rules and writing style in one file, so everyone on the team ships the same quality.

Which task keeps coming back for your team? Tell me in the comments, and send this to your team 📌

carousels.hook: Want to know why your idea will fail?
carousels.caption:
Want to know why your idea will fail?

Most of the time the problem isn't the idea. It's starting in the wrong order.

1. Building before you know anyone will pay
2. Building for everyone at once
3. Only asking friends
4. Building every feature on day one

The rule is simple: get one person to pay, then build big.

Which mistake is your idea stuck on? Drop the number in the comments, and save this for next time 💡

graphics.hook: Nobody reads your posts because your first line is weak
graphics.caption:
Nobody reads your posts because your first line is weak
On Facebook, people see only the first few lines before 'See more'
That's where they decide: read on or keep scrolling

Before you write a first line, check three things:
• Will readers recognise their own problem?
• Is there a specific moment or number?
• Did you cut the greeting and the intro?

Weak: Today I want to talk about something important
Strong: Clients leave when they hear your price? It's not the price, it's your first message

Drop the first line of your last post in the comments
